tasks.short: Check alarm details and camera images, go to the scene and investigate, coordinate guards and police, write the incident report, and decide on follow-up.

steps.what: Security supervisor checks alarm details and camera images at the control desk
Security supervisor investigates disturbances such as alarms, altercations and suspicious activity on the premises
Security supervisor coordinates guards and police by radio and phone
Security supervisor writes the incident report: from notes afterwards today, in a phone form with the alarm's time stamps and location filled in after the change
Security supervisor decides on follow-up

tasks.design: Each alarm event in the alarm system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) opens the linked camera view and the location on the site plan, so the supervisor does not search camera feeds. The incident report is a structured form on a phone with time stamps from the alarm event, photos and fixed fields, instead of a report written from notes afterwards. Investigating, coordinating and deciding follow-up stay with the supervisor. No software analyses behaviour or faces.
tasks.previous_blocker: Camera feeds were searched by hand and reports written from notebooks.
tasks.enabler_now: Alarm systems link events to cameras; mobile incident forms are common.
tasks.still_hard: Many alarms are false and still need a visit.
tasks.human_edge: Calming an altercation before it turns violent.

evidence.claim: Alarm systems can link events to camera views and site plans; mobile incident forms can take time stamps and photos.
Emotion recognition at work is banned under AI Act article 5.

assumptions: Boundary: from the alarm or report to follow-up decided; police investigation is outside.
Input contract: cameras linked to alarm zones; fallback is searching feeds.

Investigating, coordinating and deciding follow-up keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because the camera view opens with the alarm and watching it stays; s4 keeps 75 because times, location and fixed fields fill in and the supervisor still writes what happened.
research_questions: Are incident reports complete more often?

incremental.description: Security supervisor keeps camera-to-zone links current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most incidents come in by phone or a guard's report, not as an alarm event, so the camera and times do not fill in (3.2); high: most incidents start as alarm events (7.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Patrol the premises, record checkpoint rounds, note findings in the patrol log, and hand over at shift change.

steps.what: Security supervisor patrols the premises to prevent intrusion and protect property
Security supervisor records checkpoint rounds: by signing paper lists today, by scanning the tag at each checkpoint with the phone after the change
Security supervisor notes findings during the round: in the paper patrol log today, on the phone with a photo after the change
Security supervisor hands over at shift change

tasks.design: Checkpoints carry NFC tags that the guard's phone scans, so the guard tour system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) logs rounds without paper lists. Findings are entered on the phone with a photo and the checkpoint location. Patrolling and handing over stay with the supervisor. Tour logs are used to show rounds were walked, not to rate staff speed, unless the works council agrees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rounds were signed on paper lists and findings written in a logbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Guard tour systems with NFC tags and mobile forms are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Phones fail in cold or wet weather.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a door that is closed but should not be.

reach.learn: Whether rounds are walked as agreed.

evidence.claim: Guard tour systems log checkpoints by NFC tag scans with mobile forms.
Staff monitoring needs works council consent under WOR article 27(1)(l).

assumptions: Boundary: from the patrol schedule to the shift handed over; incident response is outside.
Input contract: tags fitted at checkpoints; fallback is paper lists.
Patrolling, noting findings (a first record) and handing over keep their full time. s2 keeps 20 for scanning each tag.
Works council consent and a DPIA come before tour logging.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tags are fitted at only half of the checkpoints, so paper lists stay for the rest (3.5); high: all checkpoints tagged (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check visitors' identity and appointment, write details in the logbook, issue and collect badges, decide on entry for unexpected persons, and monitor access alarms.

steps.what: Host pre-registers the visitor with name, date and host in the visitor system
Security supervisor checks visitors' identity and appointment at reception
Security supervisor records visitor details: in the paper logbook today; after the change only visitors who were not pre-registered are entered in the visitor system
Security supervisor issues and collects badges
Security supervisor authorizes entry of unexpected persons
Security supervisor monitors access control alarms for employees

tasks.design: Hosts pre-register their visitors in a visitor system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which sends the visitor a QR code; at reception the supervisor scans the code, checks the ID against the name and prints the badge, so details are not asked and written in a logbook. Deciding on unexpected persons and monitoring access alarms stay with the supervisor. No face recognition is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every visitor's details were asked at the desk and written in a logbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Visitor systems with pre-registration and QR codes are common in offices.
tasks.still_hard: Many visitors arrive without being registered.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the visitor whose story does not add up.

reach.learn: Whether visitors wait less at reception.

evidence.claim: Visitor systems with pre-registration, QR codes and badge printing are common in offices.
Real-time remote biometric identification is restricted under AI Act article 5; here no face recognition is used.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visitor arrival to access monitored; employee badges are outside.
Input contract: hosts pre-register visitors; fallback is the logbook.
Hosts spend a little time registering each visitor (s0, share 1); this is other-role time outside the supervisor's savings and replaces the call reception makes to the host today.
Visitor data are deleted after a set period.

Badges, unexpected persons and access alarms keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because the call to the host to confirm the appointment goes for pre-registered visitors and the ID check stays; s2 keeps 20 because about 85% of visitors are pre-registered and the rest are entered by hand.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the supervisor: entering visitors who were not pre-registered is kept in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: hosts pre-register only about half of visitors (12.7); high: about 85% pre-registered as assumed (23.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect patrol notes, write the patrol report, check it, send it to the client, and file it.

steps.what: Security supervisor collects patrol notes from the shift
Security supervisor writes reports documenting observations made while on patrol
Security supervisor checks the final report: each finding and incident against the guards' entries, and the client contact it goes to
Security supervisor sends the checked report to the client: by e-mail today, by one send from the guard tour system after the change
Security supervisor files the report in the shared folder

tasks.design: Patrol findings, checkpoint logs and incident forms entered on phones during the shift ({OPS_SYSTEM}) are assembled into the shift report by a fixed template, so the supervisor writes only the narrative for incidents. No model drafts the narrative. The supervisor checks the report against the guards' entries and the recipient, sends it to the client, and it is filed in the records system without a separate step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were written from notebooks, mailed and filed by hand.
tasks.still_hard: Guards who skip entries leave gaps.
tasks.human_edge: Writing what a client needs to know about a pattern of incidents.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks assembled reports instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Anchorage police ended a three-month trial of AI-drafted reports: reviewing drafts ate the time saved.
In a Dutch Innovatiewet pilot, short police reports plus camera footage gave no net drop in workload because compiling footage added work.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift ended to the report filed; client follow-up is outside.
Input contract: guards enter findings on phones; fallback is notebooks.

The supervisor checks every report in full. s1 keeps 50 for reading the guards' entries and asking for missing ones; s2 keeps 60 because copying guards' findings into the report goes and the supervisor still writes the narrative; sending keeps 20; filing goes because the report already sits in the records system.
Client contacts read reports as before.
research_questions: Do clients get reports the same day more often?

incremental.description: Security supervisor chases guards for missing entries.

approvals.approved_version: The shift report exactly as checked by the supervisor in s3, sent once to the client's named contact for that site; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: guards keep notebooks on about half of shifts, so notes are still collected and copied (28.0); high: guards enter findings on phones as designed (43.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The security supervisor keeps investigating, patrolling and deciding on entry; camera searching, paper logs and written reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time on the floor.
